findings.issue: The stop-order item states the review iteration floor unconditionally: any run below min_iterations returns CONTINUE with minIterationsNotReached. convergence.cjs guards the floor with `minIterations > 1`, so a floor of 1 (or 0) never blocks a candidate and the run falls through to the legal-stop gates. Verified by calling buildStopDecision with minIterations=1, iterationCount=0, a clean all_dimensions_clean candidate: the result is BLOCKED/blockedStop, not CONTINUE/minIterationsNotReached; with minIterations=2 the same input returns CONTINUE/minIterationsNotReached.

fix.new: 4a. if min_iterations > 1 and iteration_count < min_iterations: CONTINUE (minIterationsNotReached).

findings.issue: The Tier 1 config shape enumerates the anti-convergence keys as `antiConvergence.convergenceMode` and `antiConvergence.depthMode` and omits `antiConvergence.minIterations`, the review iteration floor this topic ships. The floor is a real config key: the review config template sets it to 2 and convergence.cjs reads config.minIterations (falling back to antiConvergence.minIterations) as the floor that holds a stop candidate below the cap. The same omission repeats in the consolidated-prompt Defaults line, so a reader building the config from this presentation never learns the run has a floor.
